independent_model_review.conclusion: The 2020 guideline supports the listed criteria as historical source text, but does not establish a current landholding cutoff. The user authorized a synthetic mock implementation against this dated baseline; that does not constitute policy approval or establish current eligibility.

The second review is not human approval, legal advice, or proof of policy currentness.

runtime_safety.reason: The eligible result means only that supplied synthetic answers meet the listed 2020 mock criteria. Every result states that the current landholding cutoff and State/UT records are not verified; it is not an official decision.

rules.claim: A farmer family comprises husband, wife, and minor children and owns cultivable land as per the land records of the concerned State or Union Territory.
A farmer family is excluded when a member belongs to a listed former or present constitutional, ministerial, legislative, municipal-corporation mayor, or district-panchayat chairperson category.
Specified serving or retired government, public-sector, autonomous-institution, and local-body employees are excluded, subject to the stated MTS, Class IV, and Group D exceptions.
Specified superannuated or retired pensioners receiving monthly pension of Rs. 10,000 or more are excluded, subject to the stated employee-category exception.
Persons who paid income tax in the last assessment year are excluded.
Specified registered professionals who carry out their profession are excluded.
NRI landholding farmer families are excluded when uploaded as new beneficiaries.
A current landholding cutoff and rules for subsequent transfers or inheritance must be established before eligibility can be decided.
rules.note: The 2020 guideline sets a 2019 cutoff and says it applies for the next five years. A current replacement or extension has not been verified, so the mock cannot establish current official eligibility.
